SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CARING FOR ANIMALS ENVIRONMENT
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Caring for Animals environment helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT ANIMALS
Animals are living things. They move, feed, grow, and respond to their surroundings.
Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).
Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).
In Kenya you may see cows in a homestead, fish at a market, or birds on the school field.
Safety: do not touch unknown animals; wash hands after handling pets or farm animals.

PART 1: Identify types of waste in  In groups or pairs,

What this means
In this part you learn to identify types of waste in  In groups or pairs,. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify types of waste in  In groups or pairs,.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Caring for Animals environment” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify types of waste in  In groups or pairs,. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Sort out different types of school waste in the school  Using videos, pictures and photographs, environment for safe

What this means
In this part you learn to sort out different types of school waste in the school  Using videos, pictures and photographs, environment for safe. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: sort out different types of school waste in the school  Using videos, pictures and photographs, environment for safe.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Caring for Animals environment matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can sort out different types of school waste in the school  Using videos, pictures and photographs, environment for safe. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Caring for Animals environment is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).

Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Caring for Animals environment” around your school. (skill: identify types of waste in  In groups or pairs,)

Example 2: Say why Caring for Animals environment matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: sort out different types of school waste in the school  Using videos, pictures and photographs, environment for safe)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Caring for Animals environment to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify types of waste in  In groups or pairs,.
3. Practise this skill: sort out different types of school waste in the school  Using videos, pictures and photographs, environment for safe.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Caring for Animals environment from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Caring for Animals environment: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Caring for Animals environment?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Caring for Animals environment means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify types of waste in  In groups or pairs,.
5. Be able to: sort out different types of school waste in the school  Using videos, pictures and photographs, environment for safe.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
